definition: A small instruction-tuned checkpoint, used by both sources as the model on which a method or measurement is characterized in detail before being applied more widely. One reports the widest probe-output gap of its 18-model sweep here — cultural identity linearly readable at 0.79 while generation reaches 0.09, a gap of 0.70 — making it the clearest case that the loss is at the readout rather than the representation. The other runs all of its diagnostic analyses on this model: the learning-rate sensitivity comparison, the layer-position sweep placing the usable latent space at 25 to 50 percent of depth, and the token-level gradient attribution that lands on reasoning connectors. Both then check the finding on larger models without repeating the detail.

evidence.note: Builds a parallel entity grid of 27 folk-narrative motifs across 10 cultures and instruments 18 models with probing, logit lens, activation patching and generation, finding that the residual stream separates cultures cleanly in every model while the readout collapses onto Greco-Roman defaults — so the failure is at the decoder, not the encoder.
evidence.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs

evidence.note: Inserts optimizable latent states at an intermediate Transformer layer rather than at the output, so self-attention makes every continuation token's log-probability differentiable with respect to every latent and reward-weighted gradients reach them from the whole continuation instead of only through their own decoded token.
evidence.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning

name: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
